title: Tech Note: Bar Codes
author: Eric Juhel, 4D Developer
featured_technology: UPC and EAN-13 bar code encoding
GET PICTURE FROM LIBRARY / LIST TO ARRAY choice-list lookups
Modulo checksum calculation for control characters

historical_commentary.text: Eric Juhel's note shows a clever, low-level technique for generating scannable bar codes purely from 4D's picture library and array/string manipulation: a single black and a single white 1x1 pixel picture are horizontally concatenated and vertically stretched to build Code 39, Code 128, UPC, and EAN-13 symbols entirely without a plug-in. Bar codes and this general automatic-identification use case remain extremely common today, so the topic itself is still directly relevant, but 4D has long since gained plug-ins, bar code fonts, and later native rendering/PDF capabilities that make this manual pixel-concatenation approach unnecessary; most modern 4D bar code needs are met with a bar code font or a dedicated component instead of hand-rolled picture math.
related_updates: Modern 4D applications typically generate bar codes with dedicated bar code fonts or components rather than hand-building them pixel-by-pixel from the picture library as shown here
Bar codes remain in widespread real-world use (alongside QR codes and RFID), so the underlying need this note addresses is still relevant even though the implementation technique is dated
